newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS STAY UNBEATEN, KEEP RANGERS WINLESS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS STAY UNBEATEN, KEEP RANGERS WINLESS.

text.p: Andy Moog made 30 saves and two potentially tying goals were disallowed in the third period as the unbeaten Dallas Stars edged the winless New York Rangers 2-1 Thursday.

Benoit Hogue and Brent Gilchrist scored early in the second period for Dallas, whose 3-0 start matches the best in franchise history. The Stars also won their first three games in 1991-92 and 1979-80, but have never gone 4-0 to open the season.
"For two periods, we played very sound, disciplined hockey," said Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock." In the third, we were nervous and panicky, but overall I'm happy with the effort."

Dallas was protecting a 2-1 lead with just under five minutes left in regulation when Alexei Kovalev's centering pass from behind the net deflected past Moog off the left skate of New York's Adam Graves.
After a video review, referee Terry Gregson waved off the goal, ruling Graves was in the crease.
"He was standing in the crease. They saw it and reviewed it," Moog said. "There was no contact, he just stood there. They think it's a controversial play, but it's no-goal, period."
"Well, his one foot was in the crease," New York coach Colin Campbell said. "It's a tough way not to get a point,"
It was the second Rangers goal disallowed in the third period. With 11:59 to go, Gregson ruled he had blown the whistle just before Niklas Sundstrom poked the puck through Moog's pads.
Hogue had a goal and an assist, while former Ranger Pat Verbeek assisted on both goals for Dallas, which won for just the second time in its last 10 games at New York.
Wayne Gretzky scored his first goal as a Ranger, but New York fell to 0-2-2, its worst start since 1986-87.
"It's mostly disappointing more than anything," Gretzky said.
"We didn't really create anything. We're getting ourselves into trouble and we have to fight back."
The Rangers played without captain Mark Messier, who sat out the final game of his two-game suspension for checking from behind against Florida on Sunday.
In Philadelphia, Rod Brind'Amour's goal 33 seconds into overtime erased an embarrassing third period as the Flyers blew a three-goal lead but came away with a 5-4 victory over the Los Angeles Kings.
Mikael Renberg broke into the offensive zone and set up at the left faceoff circle. He slid a cross-ice pass to Brind'Amour, who beat goaltender Byron Dafoe with a wrist shot low to the stick side.

The Kings, who rallied from a 4-1 deficit with 8:30 remaining, knotted the contest with 4:59 to play on Ray Ferraro's first goal of the season. Doug Zmolek and Brent Grieve also scored for the Kings in the period.
Chris Therien, Karl Dykhuis, Dainius Zubrus and Eric Desjardins scored the other Philadelphia goals while Ian Laperriere had Los Angeles's first tally.
Philadelphia was without Ron Hextall, who came down with a case of the flu, and superstar centre Eric Lindros, who has a groin injury.
The Kings were 0-for-6 on the power play and managed just 13 shots over the first 40 minutes in dropping their third straight.

At Colorado, Teemu Selanne capped a five-point effort by scoring with 42 seconds left in regulation, rallying the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim from a four-goal deficit in the third period into a 6-6 tie with the Avalanche.

Selanne fired a blast from the top of the left faceoff circle through goaltender Patrick Roy's pads for his second goal of the game. He added three assists for the Ducks, who are unbeaten in their last three games (1-0-2).
Anaheim erased a 6-2 deficit by scoring four times over the final 9:16 on goals by Kevin Todd, Selanne, Warren Rychel and Selanne again.
Peter Forsberg had two goals and an assist for the Avalanche.

In Phoenix, Nikolai Khabibulin made 24 saves and four different players scored goals to lead the Coyotes to a 4-1 victory over the San Jose Sharks in the first regular-season game at America West Arena.
The Coyotes, who were the Winnipeg Jets last season, played their first home game after opening the season at Hartford and Boston.
Kris King, Mike Gartner, Shane Doan and Craig Janney scored for Phoenix.
Bernie Nicholls scored San Jose's lone goal.
